\section{Free carriers excitation}

Current experimental methods for generating femtosecond lasers in the near-ultraviolet (NUV) range remain complex, limiting research into the linear optical transitions of wide-bandgap dielectric materials such as $\mathrm{SiO}_2$.

Given these experimental limitations, research focuses primarily on studying nonlinear absorption processes that generate free carriers into the conduction band. Reacting to the electrical field, these electrons increase their energy and trigger effects such as avalanche ionization, which alter the material's optical properties, particularly its absorbance \cite{mao2004, bulgakova2010}.

In this section, we will explain the nonlinear mechanisms behind free-carrier generation, that is, the excitation of electrons from the valence band to the conduction band. In wide-bandgap dielectrics, these carriers are central to the light-matter interaction, as they provide the only means of transferring light energy to the material's crystal lattice, which is otherwise transparent to low-intensity light.
